items.title: 10.8 Mass of a substance deposited during electrolysis

blocks.text: The mass of a substance produced at an electrode during electrolysis is proportional to the time for which a constant current passes and to the strength of the current. Combining current and time: Q = I x t, where Q is the charge in coulombs (C), I the current in amperes (A) and t the time in seconds (s). The mass produced at, or removed from, an electrode is proportional to the quantity of electricity in coulombs passed through the electrolyte.

blocks.title: The Faraday
blocks.text: The quantity of electricity is often expressed in Faradays (symbol F). One Faraday is the quantity of electric charge carried by 1 mole of electrons or 1 mole of singly charged ions; its value is 96500 C mol-1.

During the electrolysis of silver nitrate solution silver is deposited at the cathode, Ag+(aq) + e- giving Ag(s), 1 mol of ions, 1 mol of electrons and 1 mol of metal: 1 Faraday (96500 C) deposits 1 mole of silver. During the electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution, Cu2+(aq) + 2e- giving Cu(s), 2 moles of electrons are needed per mole of copper, so 2 Faradays (2 x 96500 C) deposit 1 mole of copper. The number of Faradays equals the number of moles of electrons gained or lost.

blocks.prompt: How many Faradays deposit 108 g of silver, 63.5 g of copper and 27 g of aluminium (exercise Q.2i)?
blocks.explanation: Each mass is one mole. Ag+ needs 1 mole of electrons: 1 F. Cu2+ needs 2: 2 F. Al3+ needs 3: 3 F.

items: Q = I x t (C = A x s); mass deposited is proportional to the charge passed. 1 Faraday = 96500 C = charge of 1 mol electrons; Ag+ needs 1 F per mole, Cu2+ 2 F; Faradays = moles of electrons.
